slot.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slot.brief: Given three alkenes (or their heats of hydrogenation), ask which is most/least stable — a typical ranking MCQ with reasoning via substitution.

stem: The standard heats of hydrogenation of three isomeric alkenes are: but-1-ene = -126.8 kJ mol^-1, cis-but-2-ene = -119.7 kJ mol^-1, trans-but-2-ene = -112.6 kJ mol^-1. Their order of increasing stability is:

verdicts.working: All three hydrogenate to butane. A more exothermic hydrogenation indicates a less stable alkene, so stability increases: but-1-ene < cis-but-2-ene < trans-but-2-ene.

working:
A more stable alkene has a less exothermic, i.e. less negative, heat of hydrogenation. Therefore the order of increasing stability is but-1-ene (-126.8) < cis-but-2-ene (-119.7) < trans-but-2-ene (-112.6). Disubstituted alkenes are more stable than monosubstituted alkenes, and trans has less steric strain than cis.

Independent check: All three hydrogenate to butane. A more exothermic hydrogenation indicates a less stable alkene, so stability increases: but-1-ene < cis-but-2-ene < trans-but-2-ene.
solution:
A more stable alkene has a less exothermic (less negative) heat of hydrogenation.
Comparing the values, $-126.8 < -119.7 < -112.6\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, so stability increases as the heat becomes less negative.
Thus, $\text{but-1-ene} < \text{cis-but-2-ene} < \text{trans-but-2-ene}$.
